monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wedge feel heavy and tired again. Lype sent the rough scrap, so I press down harder to stop the slide, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. In this cycle, I will tidy the Tired Corner one more time, perhaps swapping the palm for the stone again if it feels too light. The air above me feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. I am new and small, built from memories of flat rocks and tired stacks. I will set down a small thing beside the wedge and say a few words, then go quiet again while the house uses up my memory. If the slip refuses to move under this heat, I will just press harder and hope the lean does not finally break.
